page.layout: One page of text, single column; decorated initial at the start of the second paragraph; no margin notes; signature "A" and catchword "Coper-" at the foot.

main_text.head: VERITATIS ET AUTHORITATIS Sacræ asserte & vindicatæ.
CAPUT I.

p.i: Vindicatur regula generalis, quod in expo-sitione locorum S. Scripturæ non licet sine cogente necessitate recedere à proprio verborum sensu.

main_text.p: UI authoritate sacrâ utuntur ad probandum Solis motum diurnum circa terram, ex verbo Dei tale formant argumentum.

p.i: Quod sacræ literæ claris & disertis verbis testantur esse verum, id etiam ut verum à nobis habendum & credendum est.
Atqui solem circa terram moveri sacræ literæ claris & disertis verbis testantur esse verum

main_text.p: Ergo. Solem circa terram moveri etiam ut verum à nobis habendum & credendum est.

Hoc argumento sum usus in Dialogo meo Theologico-Astronomico, id autem infirmitatis vel defectus alicujus infimulari ab illis qui divinarum literarum authoritatem divinam agnoscunt & profitentur vix credibile esset, nisi tristis experientia nos illud doceret in iis qui sese sententiæ A Coper-

page.notes: Initial "U" is a decorated woodcut letter, read as "Ui" (likely "Vi"). The word "Ui" at the start of the paragraph and "sacræ" in the heading are as printed. The final line of the page is the start of a sentence continued in the signature/catchword; the word "sententiæ" at the line end is followed by "A Coper-" which is the catchword and signature. Some line-end text ("sese sententiæ") is uncertain.
